title: Redwood discovery with Meridian Analytics
topics: batching and caching levers (KV cache, prefix caching)
hosted vs dedicated vs private deployment tradeoffs
summary: Discovery call focused on Meridian's cost constraints and how Redwood's hosted/dedicated/private options and batching/caching levers affect per-unit economics. AE + SE covered model variants, quantization, autoscaling, and suggested a benchmark pilot comparing hosted throughput vs dedicated capacity. Action items include sharing pricing sheet, security docs, and scheduling a pilot run for week of 3/16.
next_steps: Redwood to share detailed pricing spreadsheet and deployment comparison (Aaron) by 2026-03-11
Schedule pilot benchmark (hosted vs dedicated) with Meridian infra team for week of 2026-03-16 (Samira)
Customer to provide sample prompt set and QPS targets (Priya) by 2026-03-12
action_items: Aaron Liu: send pricing and cost model spreadsheet (due 2026-03-11)
Samira Patel: propose pilot plan and benchmark script (due 2026-03-13)
Priya Nair: share representative prompt set and 95th percentile latency SLO (due 2026-03-12)
transcript:
[00:00] Aaron (Redwood AE): hey everyone thanks for joining, um we wanted to focus on cost and unit economics today since you mentioned budget constraints in the intro. quick intros?
[00:08] Priya (Meridian - Head of ML): sure, priya here, we run model infra and embeddings pipelines, trying to get a handle on per request cost. mark from infra is here and luis will talk about network and capacity.
[00:18] Mark (Meridian - CTO): morning, yes cost is the blocker for our rollout.
[00:22] Aaron: great. samira, do you want to kick into how redwood differentiates on serving and cost levers?
[00:27] Samira (Redwood SE): yeah, thanks. so high level we offer hosted api, dedicated reserved pools, and private vpc/on-prem. each has different unit economics. hosted is easiest to start and has per-token billing, dedicated is committed capacity with lower per-token on sustained throughput, private is for compliance and can be either CAPEX or fixed monthly depending on on-prem vs managed.
[00:45] Priya: can you quantify the delta? like if i'm doing 100M tokens a month, what's the gap between hosted and dedicated?
[00:53] Samira: good q. rough ballpark: hosted list price for the model families we typically surface is X per 1k tokens, for sustained 100M tokens that's kinda high. with dedicated reserved capacity we can drive down per-token by 20-40% depending on utilization and batching. important caveat: your prompt shapes matter a lot. small prompts with high QPS reduce batching benefits.
[01:20] Luis: when you say batching benefits, what are the knobs? is this automatic or do we need app changes?
[01:26] Samira: two main levers: continuous batching at runtime and prefix/K V cache. continuous batching aggregates concurrent requests; it's automatic in our runtime but you can tune target latency vs batch size. kv cache is where repeated prefixes (like system prompts or context pieces) avoid re-computation. that is also supported, you just need to populate cache keys or we can auto-detect hot prefixes.
[01:49] Priya: ok, and quantization? we run mixed precision now but open to int8 if it doesn't degrade quality. how does that affect cost?
[01:56] Samira: great point. quantisization — sorry quantization — to int8 or 4bit reduces GPU memory and increases throughput per GPU which reduces per-token cost a lot for decoder models. downside is potential quality delta; we recommend running evals via Redwood Optimize to pick a profile that meets your quality bar.
[02:16] Mark: how deterministic are those gains? like do you guarantee 30% less cost if we move to dedicated plus int8?
[02:23] Aaron: we don't guarantee percentage numbers in the discovery but we can run a proof-of-concept with your prompts and measure real world delta. typical outcomes we've seen: 15-40% improvement depending on sequence length and cache hit rates.
[02:37] Priya: about cache hit rates — if our users have long tails of unique sessions does that reduce benefit?
[02:43] Samira: yes, prefix caching helps when you have repeated instructions or a small working set. for one-off long inputs the batching and kernels matter more. also we do KV cache across sessions for same user in some cases but that depends on privacy/data retention settings.
[02:59] Luis: network egress and multi-region: does that change cost? we operate in multi-region and have strict latency SLOs.
[03:06] Samira: routing and region selection do affect cost. hosted will route to nearest region but cross-region failover can add egress. dedicated can be pinned to a region to avoid cross-region egress charges. private on-prem avoids cloud egress but then you have infra costs.
[03:22] Priya: okay. what's the pricing model for hosted? is it flat per-token or tiers with discounts?
[03:28] Aaron: hosted is per-token with model-specific rates, plus embeddings units if used. we usually provide tiered volume discounts and overage rules. I'll share the specific pricing sheet after the call.
[03:38] Mark: if we do dedicated, what's the commitment cadence? monthly? annual?
[03:42] Aaron: both are options. monthly reserved pools exist, annual commitments get better unit economics. also we support burst capacity on top of reserved pools for spiky traffic.
[03:51] Priya: there's often this tradeoff: cheaper per-token but more ops overhead. how managed is dedicated? do you handle autoscaling and kernel tuning?
[03:59] Samira: we do the serving runtime, autoscaling policies, and kernel selection for you. customers manage model selection versions and some config. for private on-prem we provide automation and docs; there is more customer ops surface.
[04:12] [04:12] -> interruption (phone notification)
[04:18] Priya: can you go through a concrete example? say we have a mix: 60% short chat messages (avg 60 tokens), 30% embeddings batch jobs, 10% long generation (avg 800 tokens). how to estimate unit costs?
[04:30] Samira: short chats have less batchability, so per-token cost is higher vs long generations where batching and KV caching save. embeddings are charged per embedding unit; we optimize embeddings with batching on GPU and cheaper CPU options as well. we'd run your sample distribution through our cost model to give a projected blended cost.
[04:48] Aaron: can we capture some numbers now — rough—so Samira can run a model? what's your target monthly spend?
[04:55] Priya: ideally under $40k/month for initial rollout.
[04:58] Samira: ok with 100M tokens earlier you said, that's about 100M tokens/month. with that mix and modest cache hits, a hosted approach might be over the budget. dedicated reserved capacity probably hits that target, depending on model family. we'll put exact numbers in the spreadsheet.
[05:12] Mark: what about SLA for latency? do you tie pricing to latency SLOs?
[05:18] Aaron: we offer latency tiers and SLA-backed uptime on Dedicated. For hosted, there are best-effort latency targets and our console gives per-route latency metrics. if you need 95th percentile under 200ms, we typically recommend dedicated or pinned regions.
[05:32] Luis: curious about observability: can we get token-level cost breakdowns per route?
[05:36] Samira: yes, Redwood Console provides token-level cost and latency breakdowns, per-model and per-route. that helps you find hotspots and optimize prompts or cache.
[05:45] Priya: security and compliance: we need SOC 2 type II, SAML SSO, and customer-managed keys (KMS). what's supported?
[05:53] Aaron: we support SOC 2, SAML/SSO, RBAC, audit logs, and KMS integrations in Dedicated and Private. Hosted also supports SSO and SOC 2, but for customer-managed keys we generally recommend Private or Dedicated with VPC. we'll attach our security brief.
[06:08] Mark: ok. bench question — how do you run token-level benchmarks? do you simulate QPS and measure gpu utilization?
[06:14] Samira: yes. we use a benchmark harness that replays your prompt set at target QPS and measures latency, throughput, and GPU utilization. important to include cold-start patterns and tail latencies. we can run hosted vs dedicated comparison.
[06:27] Priya: what's required from our side to run that pilot?
[06:30] Samira: a representative prompt set, expected QPS patterns (p50/p95/p99), and success criteria (max cost/latency). we'll provide the harness and a runbook.
[06:40] Aaron: plan would be: you give prompts + QPS, we run a 48-72 hour benchmark on hosted and on a dedicated pool we configure, and then share results.
[06:49] Luis: who pays for dedicated pool during pilot?
[06:52] Aaron: for pilots we typically provide short-term dedicated capacity credits or discounted pilot rates; we'll note that in the pricing doc.
[06:58] Priya: ok cool. any gotchas with prompt caching and privacy? we have PII in prompts sometimes.
[07:04] Samira: by default we support encryption at rest and in transit. KV cache policies can be set to TTL or not store PII. for regulated data we recommend Private with customer KMS.
[07:16] Mark: you're talking about autoscaling policies - can we pin min capacity to avoid cold starts?
[07:21] Samira: yes, you can set minimum reserved instances to keep warm pools; that's common for low-latency applications.
[07:28] [07:28] Priya: what's the model catalog like? are you running open models or proprietary redwood models?
[07:33] Aaron: we host a curated set of open models and Redwood-verified profiles; we also surface some third-party vendor hosted models. model selection affects cost—larger models cost more per token but may reduce re-tries or multi-step prompting.
[07:48] Luis: and support for embeddings — you mentioned cheaper CPU options. is that automatic routing?
[07:53] Samira: yes, embeddings can be routed to CPU or GPU instance types depending on latency vs cost policy. we can recommend batching sizes for embedding jobs to reduce unit cost.
[08:03] Priya: about batching — do you expose a batching control or is it internal?
[08:08] Samira: both. defaults are automatic; we expose tunables in the route config for max batch size, latency thresholds, and burst windows.
[08:17] Mark: ok, let's talk numbers — you said you'd send a spreadsheet. what will it include?
[08:21] Aaron: it'll include hosted per-token rates by model family, dedicated example commit tiers and effective per-token math given utilization, cost modeling for quantization options, and pilot pricing. also notes on enterprise add-ons like extended retention and premium SLA.
[08:36] Priya: sample timeline: we want to decide by end of March. can you get back with numbers by next week?
[08:41] Aaron: yes we'll send pricing and a pilot proposal by 2026-03-11.
[08:44] Samira: one more technical note — caching hit rate sensitivity: if your cache hit rate is above ~30% you often see order of magnitude improvements in effective cost for short-form chat. below that it's more modest.
[09:00] Priya: that seems reasonable. do you have examples of customers that moved from hosted to dedicated and what savings they saw?
[09:07] Aaron: yes, we'll anonymize and include a couple of case studies in the follow-up. typical story: 30% reduction in per-token costs after moving to dedicated with int8 and higher cache hit.
[09:18] Mark: procurement question — do you support net-30 invoices?
[09:21] Aaron: yes for enterprise deals we do net-30/60 and support PO-based billing.
[09:26] Luis: is there a minimum committed spend for Dedicated?
[09:29] Aaron: depends on config, but there is a practical minimum to justify reserved capacity; we'll call that out in the spreadsheet.
[09:36] Priya: any concerns about vendor lock-in if we use Redwood-specific caching or runtime features?
[09:41] Samira: we try to keep model and API compatibility standard; caching and runtime optimizations are implementation details but we provide exportable artifacts and migration playbooks. still, some ops-specific configs would need adaptation if you self-host elsewhere.
[09:56] Mark: ok thanks. let's go through immediate next steps: Aaron you'll send pricing; Samira will propose pilot; Priya will send prompt set.
[10:06] Aaron: yep. scheduling note — samira, can you lead the pilot setup call with luis and mark next week?
[10:12] Samira: absolutely, I'll send a calendar invite for the pilot kickoff (aiming 2026-03-16).
[10:18] Priya: sounds good. any last questions?
[10:21] Mark: none here.
[10:23] Luis: no.
[10:24] Aaron: great, thanks everyone. we'll follow up with the docs and pricing; happy to run the benchmark.
[10:29] [END]
